sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's geothermal pipeline is accelerating via PLN's 2025-2030 RUPTL, with PGEO's direct steam contracts locking in 20-year tariff escalations that insulate cash flows from commodity volatility.
TPIA's coal-to-green-ammonia conversion leverages captive low-cost coal feedstock and export demand from Japan/Korea, creating a structural margin advantage over pure-play renewables.
Domestic biofuel mandates (B40/B50) are forcing CPO-based feedstock demand higher, favoring CDIA's integrated plantation-to-energy model over import-dependent US climate-tech peers.
sectors.ai: Buy selective geothermal and green-industrial names (PGEO, TPIA) on Indonesia's captive demand and policy tailwinds; avoid US-exposed climate-tech until rates stabilize. PGEO's +7.9% confirms upstream pricing power, while TPIA's green ammonia pivot monetizes coal-to-chemicals transition. Trim BREN/MPOW on valuation risk; add CDIA for biofuel feedstock leverage.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Small/mid-cap FMCG names are driving sector returns as institutional investors rotate out of large-cap staples into higher-beta consumer plays with clearer earnings catalysts.
Water and beverage companies (ADES, AGAR) are benefiting from structural demand growth in premium hydration and on-the-go consumption, supported by rising urban disposable income.
Packaging and plastics-linked consumer firms (PDES, INDR) are gaining on input-cost stabilization and export-driven volume recovery, offering durable margin expansion into 2025.
sectors.ai: Buy selective small/mid-cap FMCG names showing volume-price breakouts (PDES, ADES, AGAR) while large caps lag; momentum is broad but fragile, so take profits on 10%+ single-day spikes. Favor water/beverage and packaging sub-sectors for earnings visibility; avoid chasing BTEK without confirmation. Position for a 2-4 week hold as IDX consumer breadth improves, but trim if aggregate signal flips negative.

Trim US-exposed names like VRT on rate-cut delays; rotate into domestic contractors with visible government backlog.
